title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 21
statement: Let \(ABCD\) be an isosceles trapezoid with \(\overline{BC} \parallel \overline{AD}\) and \(AB = CD.\) Points \(X\) and \(Y\) lie on diagonal \(\overline{AC}\) with \(X\) between \(A\) and \(Y,\) as shown in the figure. Suppose \(\angle AXD = \angle BYC = 90^\circ,\) \(AX = 3,\) \(XY = 1,\) and \(YC = 2.\) What is the area of \(ABCD?\)

solutions.text:
Put \(A = (0,0),\) \(X = (3,0),\) \(Y = (4,0),\) \(C = (6,0).\) The right angles give \(D = (3, t)\) and \(B = (4, s)\) on opposite sides of \(AC.\)

Parallelism \(\overline{AD}\parallel\overline{BC}\) forces \(t = -\tfrac{3}{2}s,\) and \(AB = CD\) gives \(16 + s^2 = 9 + t^2,\) so \(t^2 - s^2 = 7.\) Substituting yields \(s^2 = \tfrac{28}{5}.\)

The shoelace formula gives area \(= 3\,|t - s|\) \(= 3\cdot\tfrac{5}{2}s\) \(= \tfrac{15}{2}s\) \(= \tfrac{15}{2}\sqrt{\tfrac{28}{5}}\) \(= 3\sqrt{35}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Place \(A, X, Y, C\) on a horizontal line with \(AX = 3,\) \(XY = 1,\) \(YC = 2.\) Then \(D\) is vertically below \(X\) and \(B\) vertically above \(Y\)
Use \(\overline{BC}\parallel\overline{AD}\) and \(AB = CD\) to relate the heights of \(B\) and \(D,\) then apply the shoelace formula
